whyTestArgs: Both packages, because the core's rules are pinned twice: by this crate's own tests of the core over the in-memory backend, and by the Windows driver's tests, which run a real core over a real ring, and a sabotage of the core that only the driver's tests catch would otherwise read as surviving. --no-fail-fast, so the doctests run even when the unit tests have already failed: the worked examples in win-durable-ioring's README.md are compiled as doctests and claim to break the build when a change invalidates them (DI-3.2.4); without this flag cargo stops at the first failing target, the doctests never run under any sabotage the unit tests catch, and nothing shows that claim is true.
description: Sabotages for durable-ioring, the portable core (DI-8.2); the Windows driver's are in ../win-durable-ioring/sabotage.json. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format and for why the results are read the way they are.
notCoveredHere: No test can produce these failures: durability.rs's two for states nothing produces (a completion never recorded as pushed, a flush for a seal not flushing); the durability core's debug assertions for a flush or a token it has no record of; and the oracle's AbandonedUnknown rule's lookup, which the oracle tests reach but no single-line patch can disable without also disabling the suspect-set comparison beside it. The Windows driver's own absences are in ../win-durable-ioring/sabotage.json.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.1: a domain repeated within one file counts twice
sabotages.why: A file's domains are a set; a repeat would make intersection and containment checks see a domain more than once.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.1: every instance gets the same instance id
sabotages.why: The instance id is what lets an instance refuse another's lineages, operations and failures. A repeated one makes a foreign identity indistinguishable from a native one.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.1: epochs of different lineages compare by id
sabotages.why: Epochs of two lineages are unrelated (DI-D-19); ordering them by id alone would let a seal in one lineage appear to cover another's.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.2.1: the core drops every completion
sabotages.why: One completion per operation (DI-D-24): nothing pushed would ever be reported. Every test that waits for a completion times out at its bound.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.2.1: the readiness event is set only when the queue was already non-empty
sabotages.why: The empty-to-non-empty transition is the one DI-D-28 requires: a single waiter that has popped to None sleeps until it. Caught by the readiness check's first push.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.2.1: a write is recorded as a read
sabotages.why: The write's tag is what durability will be computed from (DI-3.2.3). The oracle's kind rule catches it in every test that writes.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.2.1: operation identities are not advanced
sabotages.why: Two operations under one identity cannot be told apart. The oracle's duplicate-identity rule, and the push-order test.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.2.1: a push naming an unknown file is not refused
sabotages.why: The refusal must hand back the buffer and the context; without it the push reaches a lookup that cannot succeed.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.2.1: the oracle misses a second completion
sabotages.why: The oracle is the one definition of one-completion-per-operation; a second completion must be named as such.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.2.1: the oracle misses an identity reused after completing
sabotages.why: An identity returned again once its first operation completed would let the second's completion pass as the first's.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.2.1: the oracle ignores the kind
sabotages.why: What was pushed comes back: a completion reporting another kind or epoch is a violation.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.2.1: the oracle ignores the context
sabotages.why: The consumer's context is handed back unchanged; this is the oracle's half of that rule.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.2.1: the oracle finishes with operations outstanding
sabotages.why: A lost completion is invisible to every rule that looks at entries; only finish names it.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.3: a seal does not wait for its writes in flight
sabotages.why: Guarantee 5: a seal made before its writes complete would name no flush for them and report Durable before their completions. The durability unit tests catch it deterministically; the I/O test's oracle catches it when the kernel has not finished the writes by the seal.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.3: a seal names no flush for its writes
sabotages.why: Durable means on stable media (guarantee 1); a seal that flushes nothing reports durability the device was never asked for. No I/O test can see a flush that was not issued, which is why the rule lives in the I/O-free core and is tested there.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: a seal whose flush failed counts as successful
sabotages.why: A heal takes effect at the first seal after it that finishes successfully (DI-D-12 (c)); a seal whose own flush failed has re-issued nothing safely. Caught by the unit test whose second seal fails after a heal.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.3: a later seal is reported past a pending one
sabotages.why: The prefix property (guarantee 2): Durable through 2 covers 1, so it must wait for 1. Caught by the I/O test whose first seal a provider holds, and by the unit tests.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.3: a write a provider serves does not hold its seal
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: such a write is durable only when the provider says so. A seal that finishes on its flushes alone reports durable what nobody checked; the provider tests see Durable before any answer.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.3: an epoch below the high-water mark is not reported durable
sabotages.why: Guarantee 7: asking again about a sealed epoch reports its state, and a durable epoch reports Durable.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.3: a write at or below the seal is not refused
sabotages.why: Guarantee 6: a late write is refused before anything is reserved, with its buffer handed back. Absorbed, it would join an epoch already reported durable.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.3: no synthesized entry is appended
sabotages.why: Guarantee 4: every request is answered. The state still changes, so only the queue shows it; every seal and failure test waits for its entry and times out.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.3: the oracle accepts a write at or below the seal
sabotages.why: The oracle is the one definition of guarantee 6 the I/O tests bind to; it must name an accepted late write.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.3: the oracle lowers a seal point
sabotages.why: A seal point only rises; one lowered by a later, lower report would let a late write pass.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.3: the oracle accepts Durable for what was never sealed
sabotages.why: DI-D-9: durability is reported only for a seal. A Durable nothing asked for is a report the consumer cannot place.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.3: the oracle accepts Durable before a covered completion
sabotages.why: Guarantee 5 as the I/O tests check it: without this rule, the in-flight seal test checks only a count.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: a suspect set ignores the failure's reach
sabotages.why: DI-D-21: a failure reaches only the files whose declared domains intersect its own, and unknown files. Ignoring that over-reports, and an abandon then abandons epochs nothing put at risk. Caught by the reach tests, unit and I/O.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: a write in flight is not suspected
sabotages.why: DI-D-12 (b): suspicion is by push order, not completion; a write accepted before the failure can complete after it. Caught by the unit test with a write in flight at the failure.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: a covered write stays suspect
sabotages.why: Guarantee 3: a later failure never reaches back past a write covered successfully. Caught by the finality unit test.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: a heal takes effect at a seal made before it
sabotages.why: DI-D-12 (c): only a seal made after the heal covers what was re-issued before it. Caught by the unit test whose seal predates the heal.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: abandoning does not abandon the failure's epochs
sabotages.why: DI-D-12 (f): an epoch is abandoned if any failure containing it was. Reported Durable instead, the consumer would believe lost writes are on the media. Caught by the state assertions, unit, I/O and the worked examples.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: no failure holds the high-water mark
sabotages.why: DI-D-12 (f): an epoch passes only when every failure containing it is resolved. Caught everywhere a failure is expected to block, and by the oracle's Durable-through-failure rule.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: Blocked is never appended
sabotages.why: DI-D-13: a request whose flushes succeeded but which a failure holds is answered Blocked, never left silent. Caught by the Blocked tests, unit and I/O.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: a foreign token is resolved
sabotages.why: DI-D-12 (d): another instance's token is refused, and the call hands every token back. Caught by the refusal tests; resolving it trips the debug assertion for a token with no failure.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: the inventory hands out a second live token
sabotages.why: DI-D-12 (d): at most one live token per failure. Caught by the token tests.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: the oracle lets Durable pass an unresolved failure
sabotages.why: The oracle's statement of DI-D-12 (f), which the I/O tests bind to.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: the oracle accepts a suspect it never saw pushed
sabotages.why: A suspect write must be one the instance accepted, with the epoch it was tagged with.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: the oracle accepts suspects out of push order
sabotages.why: DI-D-12 (b) lists a suspect set in push order, which the retention layer relies on for newest-wins replay (DI-D-6).

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: the oracle accepts a suspect already durable
sabotages.why: Finality, guarantee 3, as the oracle checks it.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4: the oracle accepts Blocked by any live failure
sabotages.why: Blocked names a failure at or below the request; one above it cannot be what holds it.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4.1: a write into an abandoned epoch is not refused
sabotages.why: DI-D-35: an abandoned epoch's writes were declared lost, so a write joining it would be reported with an epoch that can never be durable. Caught by the I/O test that writes into an abandoned open epoch.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4.1: the oracle accepts a write into an abandoned epoch
sabotages.why: The oracle's statement of DI-D-35, which the I/O tests bind to.

sabotages.name: WT-2.2.2: every failure is stamped with the first failure's reading, not the clock
sabotages.why: The stamp is the one thing the clock is held for. A core that never reads it reports a time that says nothing about when the failure was observed.

sabotages.name: WT-2.2.2: the inventory reports a reading taken when asked
sabotages.why: The second time fact: the inventory reports the stamp the Failed entry carried. Re-reading the clock would report when the consumer asked, which drifts from the entry and from every other record of the failure.

sabotages.name: WT-2.2.2: the oracle accepts a stamp that went backwards
sabotages.why: The first time fact, as the oracle checks it. Without the comparison every stamp is accepted, and a mock that broke its promise or a core that read its clock outside the lock would pass unnoticed.

sabotages.name: WT-2.2.2: the oracle refuses equal stamps
sabotages.why: The other direction of the same guard: interrupt time repeats a value for a whole system tick, so two failures in one tick carry equal stamps, and an oracle that refused them would reject a correct stream.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4.2: a suspect write that completes failed is not nullified
sabotages.why: The nullifier is the marking DI-D-36 exists for: without it a failure's record says nothing of a suspect write that did not happen, and reconciling the history after the fact is guesswork.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4.2: a flush covers every write of its seal, not its own file's
sabotages.why: Coverage is per file (DI-D-39): a seal that failed on one file has not committed that file's writes, so marking them covered -- and dropping them as covered -- is a wrong answer about what is on the device.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.2: a covered marking cites the flush and the provider the wrong way round
sabotages.why: A covered marking cites who answered (DI-D-47): the default's flush, which dioring observed, or the provider, whose answer is its own warranty. Swapping them attributes a provider's warranty to an observed flush, which is exactly the misportrayed provenance the engineer ruled out.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.2: a covered marking never cites the provider
sabotages.why: A write the provider covered must say so: information that came from a durability provider is cited as the provider's (DI-D-47). A marking that always reads as the default's flush hides that the warranty was the consumer's.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.2: a covered marking always cites a flush
sabotages.why: A file only the provider serves had no flush of dioring's; a marking claiming one reports an observation dioring never made (DI-D-47).

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4.2: only the first failure suspecting a write is marked
sabotages.why: Failures and writes are many-to-many: a write two failures suspect belongs to both records, and each must say what happened to it.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4.2: a marking finds only the first suspect write
sabotages.why: The lookup is what ties a completion to the failures suspecting it; one that sees only the first write of each set loses the rest.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4.2: a heal takes effect without its Healed entry
sabotages.why: A heal's final record is the one DI-D-36 found missing: the failure leaves the inventory, and with no entry its record is lost.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4.2: the inventory reports no markings
sabotages.why: The inventory is where a consumer reads a live failure's record; reporting it without its markings hides what the stream already said.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.2: the oracle accepts a nullifier with any fault
sabotages.why: A nullifier relays the one report its write's completion carried (DI-D-50); an oracle comparing kinds and not faults lets a wrong code, or another report, through.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: the oracle holds Durable for a healed failure until its Healed entry
sabotages.why: Inverted by DI-D-42: a heal takes effect in each lineage separately (DI-D-41), so one lineage's Durable may pass a failure the consumer healed before the failure's Healed entry, which waits for every lineage it held. Restoring DI-D-39's tighter rule would reject that legal stream. Caught by the oracle's own test and by the ring test of a failure spanning two lineages.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4.2: the oracle accepts an Abandoned record with other markings
sabotages.why: A final record is the record: one whose markings differ from those the stream reported is two histories of one failure.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.4.2: a Win32 code is not masked to sixteen bits when wrapped
sabotages.why: HRESULT_FROM_WIN32 keeps only the low sixteen bits; carrying more would set facility bits and name a different code.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: a covered write is recognised with its conditions reordered
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself. The conditions are pure and independent, so their order changes no answer.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the clock is read before the token is minted
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself. Minting the token and freezing the suspect set read no clock and cannot move one, and all of it happens inside the one transition under the lock, so reading the clock first changes no stamp.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: ending a lineage abandons nothing
sabotages.why: DI-D-30: every epoch not yet durable is abandoned, and LineageEnded says through which. Caught by the core tests that end a lineage with sealed, written and in-flight epochs.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: an ended lineage stays live
sabotages.why: DI-D-42: an ended lineage is not live from the moment it ends, though it stays recorded while its writes in flight drain; answering for it then would report state the instance no longer keeps. Caught by the core tests that query a draining lineage.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: a heal takes effect in every lineage at the first one's seal
sabotages.why: DI-D-41: each lineage's re-issued writes are committed only by its own next seal, so one lineage's seal ending the failure everywhere lets another's mark pass epochs it has not committed -- a wrong answer. sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: a heal never releases a lineage it reached
sabotages.why: DI-D-41: once a lineage's next seal succeeds after the heal, the failure stops holding that lineage, whose mark may pass it before the failure is healed everywhere. Caught by the tests whose first lineage reports Durable while the failure still holds the second.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: ending a lineage does not release a heal waiting for it
sabotages.why: DI-D-42: a lineage that ends will never seal again, so a heal waiting for its seal would wait forever. Caught by the core and ring tests that end the lineage a heal still waits for.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: a failure observed after the end suspects the ended lineage's writes
sabotages.why: DI-D-30: an ended lineage answers nothing more, and a failure belongs to every lineage it suspects -- one that has ended could never resolve its part. Caught by the core test that observes a failure after the end, and the oracle's rule.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: an import scoped to a lineage is not confined to it
sabotages.why: DI-D-19: ImportScope::Lineage narrows a failure to that lineage's writes. Widened, it would hold other lineages' marks for a failure the consumer placed in one. Caught by the ring test that imports into each of two lineages.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: retiring ignores a failure holding the lineage
sabotages.why: DI-D-30: retiring abandons nothing, so it must be refused while an unresolved failure holds the lineage, or that failure's epochs there would be dropped unresolved. Caught by the core test whose lineage is held by a failure alone.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: retiring ignores writes in flight
sabotages.why: DI-D-30: a lineage with writes in flight is not empty; retiring it would forget writes whose completions are still to come. Caught by the core test that retires with a write in flight.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: a flush answering after its lineage ended is reported
sabotages.why: DI-D-30: a flush that finishes after the end reports nothing. Answered, it finds the ended lineage's seals cleared and records an inconsistency. Caught by the core test whose flush answers while the lineage drains a write in flight.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: a lineage key is reused
sabotages.why: DI-D-19: a lineage is never reused, including after retirement, so a name a consumer kept never comes to mean another lineage. Caught by the core tests that mint twice.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: a handle consumed by end_lineage stays armed
sabotages.why: Disarming is what stops the last handle, consumed by end_lineage or retire_lineage, from ending the lineage again as it is released: the release ends it first, and end_lineage then finds it already ended, an inconsistency reported and panicked on (DI-D-46). Silently ignored, as the swap first had it, the double end is invisible and this entry survives -- which is how that was found. First recorded as an equivalent CONTROL, on the argument that a release finds the lineage no longer live; running it hung, because retire_lineage then consumed the handle under the core's lock, which a release takes. It now releases the lock first. Caught by the ring tests of end_lineage.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the abandoned-through bound takes its operands in the other order
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself. The maximum of two values does not depend on their order.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: the oracle accepts a lineage ended twice
sabotages.why: The oracle's statement that a lineage ends once. Caught by its own test.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.1: the oracle accepts Durable for an ended lineage
sabotages.why: The oracle's statement that an ended lineage answers nothing more. Caught by its own test.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.2: a gate reached releases nothing

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.2: operations released together go in gate order
sabotages.why: DI-D-43: operations released at once are pushed in push order, whatever epoch each waited for, so a release reorders nothing the consumer pushed. Caught by the core push-order test.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.2: a seal does not wait for the held writes it covers

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.2: an issued write is not recorded in flight

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.2: a seal cycle is not looked for

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.5.2: a gate on a lineage the instance cannot answer for is held

sabotages.why: DI-D-27: a failure of domain D reaches the files whose domains contain D and the unknown ones. Reaching every file suspects writes in other domains, which is a wrong answer about what is at risk.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: an answer for an ended lineage is applied
sabotages.why: DI-D-42 and DI-D-44: an ended lineage is not live, and a late answer for it reports nothing. Applying it observes a failure for a lineage the instance no longer answers for.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: a second answer for a domain is applied
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: each domain is answered once. A second answer would change a recorded outcome, and observe a failure after a success was already acted on.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: a domain the provider does not serve is asked about
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: the default answers for every domain the provider does not serve. Asking the provider about one makes the seal wait for an answer the provider owes nobody.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: a request's domains are not sorted
sabotages.why: DI-D-44: a request names its domains in the order of their interned ids. The request test pushes a file declared out of order, so the order of first appearance differs.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: a request's domains are sorted stably
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself. A seal's parts name each domain once, so a stable sort orders them as the unstable one does.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: a seal records no domain it asked about
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: the seal waits for every domain it asked about. Recording none lets it finish on its flushes, and refuses every answer as one it did not ask for.
replace:
let domains: Vec<SealDomain> = Vec::new();
            let _: Vec<SealDomain> = parts

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.6: a completion dropped unanswered answers nothing
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: a completion dropped unanswered is a failure of its domain. Without it the seal stays pending forever and the consumer is never told, which guarantee 4 forbids.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: a file with operations held for a gate is removed
sabotages.why: API.md section 8: a held operation is pushed to its file later, so removing the file strands it.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: the lowest gate kept is the highest
sabotages.why: IoTargetBusy.lowest_gates names the lowest gate in each lineage: the first a consumer must make durable.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: an equal gate replaces the lowest
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself. Two gates with the same id in one lineage are the same epoch, so replacing one with the other changes no report.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: a failure does not hold its file
sabotages.why: API.md section 8: every write in an unresolved failure's suspect set holds its file, since healing it re-issues writes there.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: a suspect write is also counted as uncovered
sabotages.why: IoTargetBusy.uncovered is outside every failure's suspect set; a suspect write is reported through its failure, and counting it twice tells the consumer to seal what sealing cannot clear.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: a write in flight is also counted as uncovered
sabotages.why: A write in flight is the I/O core's to count; counting it here too reports it twice.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: the epoch to seal through is the lowest, not the highest
sabotages.why: IoTargetBusy.uncovered_through is what to seal through to clear every uncovered write; the lowest would clear only some.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: every failure is said to hold every file
sabotages.why: A failure holds a file only when its suspect set names a write to it; reporting the rest asks the consumer to resolve failures that do not concern the file.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: a completion never clears its file's last operation
sabotages.why: DI-D-45: in_flight clears as completions arrive. A count left at one refuses the file forever.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: close hands back no held operation
sabotages.why: DI-D-25: close() returns the gated operations the kernel never saw, with their buffers and contexts; dropping them loses the consumer's buffers.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: close hands back no failure
sabotages.why: DI-D-25: close() returns the unresolved failures.

sabotages.name: DI-3.2.7: a completion is not counted when made
sabotages.why: DI-D-45: ending waits until the count is zero, so an uncounted completion is not waited for, and its answer is recorded as an inconsistency.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.1: a heal is released by a seal that stops short of the re-issue
sabotages.why: DI-D-46: the releasing seal must reach the highest epoch pushed when the heal was made, or the mark passes the failed epoch while the re-issued writes are not committed.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.1: a write in flight is not part of the re-issue
sabotages.why: DI-D-46: the re-issue is every write pushed before the heal. Without the pushed one, a seal short of it releases the heal.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.1: a held write is not part of the re-issue
sabotages.why: DI-D-46: a held write counts as pushed, so the releasing seal waits for it to be released and complete.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.1: an unmatched import domain is not reported
sabotages.why: DI-D-46: a domain the instance was never given is reported, so a misspelling is not silent.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.1: an inconsistency is not panicked on
sabotages.why: DI-D-46: an inconsistency is panicked on where it is found, in every build; carrying on would report from bookkeeping known to be wrong.

sabotages.name: DI-3.9.1: an inconsistency panics while unwinding
sabotages.why: DI-D-46 and the ring crate's D-79: a second panic while unwinding aborts the process and loses the first. The test binary aborts, which the harness counts as caught.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.3: an inconsistency is not reported to the sink
sabotages.why: DI-D-51 routes the inconsistency report through the consumer's sink; dropping it leaves a consumer who chose stderr, OutputDebugString or ETW with a panic and nothing in the place it watches.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.3: the core reports to a sink without asking whether it wants the event
sabotages.why: Asking first is what makes a sink that wants nothing cost a branch (DI-D-51 T2); not asking hands every event to every sink.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.3: a fan-out gives each event to every sink
sabotages.why: A fan-out hands an event only to the sinks that want its kind, so a sink's answer to wants means the same behind a fan-out as alone.
replace: for sink in self.sinks.iter().filter(|_| kind == kind) {

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.3: a fan-out wants an event only when every sink does
sabotages.why: A fan-out wants what any of its sinks wants; requiring all of them would silence a stderr sink beside a deaf one.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a full submission queue is not refused
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: a refusal names its cause. A backend that queues past its submission queue never tells the caller to submit.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a full completion queue is not refused
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: a refusal names its cause. A backend that admits more than its completion queue holds never tells the caller to drain.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a full submission queue is reported as needing a drain
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: the cause is what lets the caller act without probing; the wrong cause sends it to the wrong remedy.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a memory commit makes nothing durable
sabotages.why: A commit is what makes a memory target's bytes durable; without it a test cannot read what a commit warranted.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: the notification is raised on every submit that leaves completions
sabotages.why: DI-D-50 P10: the notification is raised on the transition from no completions to some, not on every submission.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a read past the end reports its whole buffer
sabotages.why: A read may complete short, and the count is the consumer's to handle; reporting the buffer's length claims bytes that were not read.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a buffer's address is not checked
sabotages.why: A target's geometry covers its buffers' addresses as well as its offsets and lengths; unbuffered I/O needs all three.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a submission for a detached target loses its buffer
sabotages.why: Buffers go in owned and come back (DI-D-50 P10), on a fault as on a success.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the memory backend tests emptiness by length
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the new code: an empty queue has length zero, so this is an equivalent change. If it comes back caught, something is reacting to more than behaviour.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: needing both is not reported as needing a drain
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: a caller told both must drain as well as submit; dropping the drain leaves it retrying into a full completion queue.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: an unknown refusal is called retryable
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: an unknown cause may never clear; calling it retryable invites a caller to loop on it.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a length is checked against the offset's alignment
sabotages.why: A target's offsets and lengths may need different alignments; checking one against the other admits operations the target cannot take.
find: offset.is_multiple_of(self.offset as u64) && length.is_multiple_of(self.length as u64)
replace: offset.is_multiple_of(self.offset as u64) && length.is_multiple_of(self.offset as u64)

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: zero is accepted as an alignment
sabotages.why: A Geometry always holds powers of two; zero would make every alignment check divide by zero.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.1: a description drops the target's flush domains
sabotages.why: DI-D-50 P4: the core decides failure sharing from the domains a target declares; a description without them makes every target share fate with every other.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a refused write spends an operation id
sabotages.why: Only an accepted push spends an id, so accepted pushes' ids are consecutive; a refused one is undone whole (DI-D-52).

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a refused commit is dropped
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: a commit the backend refuses is kept and emitted again; dropping it leaves its seal waiting forever.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a refused commit is not emitted with the next actions
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: a kept commit rides on the next actions, so a driver that only acts on actions still issues it.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: deliver is set whenever the queue holds entries
sabotages.why: Readiness is raised on the queue's transition from empty, as DI-D-28 sets the readiness event; raising it on every change wakes the consumer for nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a write is not recorded with the durability core
sabotages.why: A seal waits for, and commits, the writes recorded with it; one never recorded is neither waited for nor covered.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: an operation in flight is not counted against its target
sabotages.why: DI-D-45: removing a target is refused while operations on it are in flight.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a write's completion is not told to the durability core
sabotages.why: A seal commits only writes that completed; the core learns of completion here.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a failed operation is reported as a transfer
sabotages.why: A fault is reported on the operation's completion (the contract's obligations), never hidden as a zero-byte transfer.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: another core's lineage is taken for this one's
sabotages.why: DI-D-40: a lineage carries its instance, so another core's is refused rather than read as this one's of the same number.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: a target with an operation in flight is removed
sabotages.why: DI-D-45: every hold refuses removal, operations in flight among them.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.2: an accepted operation is not recorded
sabotages.why: An accepted operation is in flight until its completion, which the core must recognise; one never recorded makes its own completion a breach.
find: self.issued(token, id, kind, target, context, false);

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the core's actions test emptiness by length
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the core: an empty vector has length zero, so this is an equivalent change. If it comes back caught, something is reacting to more than behaviour.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: a released operation is not recorded as issued
sabotages.why: DI-D-23: a held write is recorded in flight once its gate releases it; one never recorded is never waited for by a seal.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: a released operation the backend refuses is not kept
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: an operation the core emitted after its gate is the core's to keep and emit again, as a commit is.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: an operation never issued is reported as transferred
sabotages.why: Guarantee 9: a held operation an abandoned epoch stopped ends as NeverIssued, naming the epoch, so the consumer knows nothing was written.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: a gate on an abandoned epoch is not refused
sabotages.why: DI-D-43: an operation gated on an abandoned epoch could never be released, so it is refused at once.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: a write closing a gate cycle is not refused
sabotages.why: DI-D-43: a write whose gate needs, transitively, the write itself would wait forever.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: a gate in another core is taken for this one's
sabotages.why: DI-D-40: an epoch carries its lineage's instance, so a gate on another core's is refused rather than read as this core's of the same number.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: an operation held for a gate does not hold its target
sabotages.why: DI-D-45: every hold refuses removal, operations held for a gate among them.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: the default lineage can be ended
sabotages.why: The default lineage never ends while the core lives.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: a busy lineage is reported retired
sabotages.why: DI-D-40: a lineage is retired only once nothing holds it, and a refusal says what does.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the core states a minted lineage's key type
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the lineage code: a lineage key is a u64, so naming the type changes nothing. If it comes back caught, something is reacting to more than behaviour.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: the core makes no requests of the provider
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: a seal touching a served domain is answered by the provider; without its request the seal never finishes.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: every provider answer is taken as success
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: a provider's failure is a failure of its domain; taking it as success reports durable what was lost.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: an answer for a domain the provider does not serve is accepted
sabotages.why: An answer the core never asked for is a protocol breach (DI-D-44); the core names it, rather than reading it as the seal's.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.3: the durability core is not told what the provider serves
sabotages.why: DI-D-27: the durability core asks the provider only for the domains it serves; without them a served target's seal waits for an answer never requested.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.4: the oracle accepts a short write
sabotages.why: DI-D-50: a write completes in full or with a fault; a short count is a target breaking its obligation.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.4: the oracle accepts a write longer than it asked
sabotages.why: A write transferring more than its length did not do what was pushed; in full means exactly.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.4: the oracle holds a read to its length
sabotages.why: A read may complete short (the contract); refusing one encodes a rule the contract does not make.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.4: the core's tests do not report their seals to the oracle
sabotages.why: The oracle runs beside the core's tests (DI-D-24); a Durable for a seal it was never told of is DurableNotSealed, which only the oracle sees -- so this proves the binding is live.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.1: a submission the backend refuses is dropped
sabotages.why: DI-D-52: a refused submission the core originated goes back to it, which keeps it and emits it again; dropped, its seal waits forever.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.1: the engine keeps no provider requests
sabotages.why: DI-D-44: the driver makes the provider's requests with its lock released, so the engine keeps them; dropped, a served seal never finishes.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.1: a drain stops after one pass
sabotages.why: The notification is an edge (the ring crate's D-19), so a drain runs until a pass pops nothing; one pass leaves what the completions made due unissued.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.1: a drain reports no readiness
sabotages.why: DI-D-28: entries made poppable by a drain must be told, or a consumer waiting on readiness waits forever.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: act rings no doorbell
sabotages.why: A backend only queues what it is pushed, so the engine's act is what issues a batch. Without the doorbell nothing is issued until a completion drives a drain, and with none in flight, never.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a push rings the doorbell for itself as well as the batch
sabotages.why: The doorbell is rung once for a batch, which is what a ring is for: a push that rings its own makes one submission per push.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a failed doorbell is not told
sabotages.why: A doorbell that fails leaves what was pushed queued, with nothing in flight to drive a drain. Not told, the consumer waits for a completion that cannot come.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a refusal for want of room is not rung and tried once more
sabotages.why: A queue that is full is cleared by the doorbell, which the engine can ring at once; without the retry the push waits for a completion to re-emit it.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a consumer's push does not note its failed doorbell
sabotages.why: The driver tells the consumer, once, that a push is queued and its doorbell failed, so the consumer's pop rings it again and reports a cause that stays.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: the note of a failed doorbell is not cleared when taken
sabotages.why: Told once: a note that is not cleared tells the consumer on every push after.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a failed read of completions is forgotten
sabotages.why: The drain that could not read its completions ends, and the consumer's pop reports why; forgotten, the consumer is not told its ring cannot be read.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: the last fault is kept in place of the first
sabotages.why: The first fault is the one that explains the rest, and a second drain failing the same way must not replace it.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a drain that could not read goes on
sabotages.why: A backend that cannot read its completions ends the drain, and the consumer is told; going on reports nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-7+.2: a fault a later read got past is still reported
sabotages.why: A read that works after a failed one makes the fault stale, which the consumer is not told. Both clearing sites are removed together: either alone leaves the other clearing it, so each is equivalent by itself.

sabotages.name: PR-126: a write ending past isize::MAX is admitted
sabotages.why: A Vec holds at most isize::MAX bytes, so a write ending past it can only panic the target; check and push refuse it as malformed. Caught by the boundary test, one byte either side of the bound.

sabotages.name: PR-126: a target that cannot grow aborts instead of reporting it
sabotages.why: A write the target cannot find memory for completes with a fault and hands its buffer back, as every allocation that can fail is reported and not aborted on. Without the try_reserve the resize aborts the process, which the sweep sees as the suite dying: a weaker detection than an assertion, and the test that names the behaviour is the one that dies.

sabotages.name: PR-126: registered buffers are replaced while an operation is outstanding
sabotages.why: A queued or finished operation may name a registered region, which replacing the buffers invalidates; the builder refuses it as a caller's programming error. Caught by the two should_panic tests, one with an operation queued and one with a completion waiting.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the engine tests a pass's pops by comparison
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the engine: negating a bool and comparing it with false are the same test. If it comes back caught, something is reacting to more than behaviour.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: an operation is held without asking the backend
sabotages.why: DI-D-54: a gated operation is put to the backend's check before it is held, so it is refused at push for what an ungated one would be. Unasked, a gated span on a backend with no registration is accepted, and fails only once released.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: every refusal of the core's own is kept
sabotages.why: DI-D-54: a submission refused for a cause that is not retryable can never be issued; kept, it is re-emitted forever and its operation never completes.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: every refusal of the core's own ends it
sabotages.why: The other direction: a full queue clears once the driver submits or drains, so a submission refused for it is kept, not failed.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: a refusal fault does not carry its cause
sabotages.why: The REFUSED fault's error is the RefusalCause itself, so a consumer can recover it by downcasting rather than parsing a message.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: a refusal fault drops the backend's code
sabotages.why: A cause carrying the backend's report keeps its code on the fault, as every fault the backend reports itself does.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: the engine does not act on what a refusal makes due
sabotages.why: A refusal that ends a submission makes its completion due -- a failure, an entry -- and the engine acts on it in the same call, so the readiness it raises is not lost.

sabotages.name: DI-3.10.3.5.6.2.1: the memory backend's check admits everything
sabotages.why: check answers what push would refuse whatever the queues hold; one that admits everything lets the core hold what it can never issue.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the engine folds readiness by a longer spelling
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the reworked act: an equivalent spelling of the same fold must survive; caught would mean a test is matching incidental code.

sabotages.name: DI-7.1: a pool drain does not submit first
sabotages.why: Each pass of a drain begins by submitting what a failed submit left queued, so a consumer that has stopped popping still gets its work issued. Without it a drain runs and never asks the ring. Caught by the drain test, which requires a failed submit on a thread other than its own.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a pump drains before it waits
sabotages.why: The wait is for the completions the drain then takes. Drained first, a pump woken by a raising returns having taken nothing, and the entries are there only for the next one.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a pump waits holding the engine's lock
sabotages.why: The wait is for something another thread does, and doing it takes the lock: a push, a provider's answer, a handle's release. Held through the wait, nothing can wake the pump but its own timeout.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a pump whose wait failed does not drain
sabotages.why: A delivery that cannot wait still delivers what has completed, and says why it could not wait. Skipping the drain makes a broken notification stop an instance delivering at all.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a pump reports the drain's result inverted
sabotages.why: Whether entries became poppable is what sets the readiness event and what a consumer's loop keys on.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a delivery's shared slot is not its own
sabotages.why: A provider's answer and a handle's release reach the engine through the slot shared out; a slot of its own finds nothing there.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a fault the backend does not keep loses its report
sabotages.why: A construction that fails names why: the backend's own report, whole, when nothing else holds it.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a fault the backend keeps loses its kind
sabotages.why: A report that cannot be taken whole is reproduced by its kind and its text, so a caller that matches on the kind still can.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a memory notification forgets what its wait saw
sabotages.why: A wait is for a raising since the last one that saw any. Forgetting makes every wait after the first return at once.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a memory notification's wait with no limit returns at once
sabotages.why: None is no limit: a wait that does not wait is a poll, and a pump with no limit would spin.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a memory notification's timeout is ignored
sabotages.why: A wait that returns before its timeout reports no raising when one was about to come.

sabotages.name: DI-7.3: a memory notification reports a raising when it timed out
sabotages.why: Whether it was raised is the answer the wait exists to give; the boundary is a count equal to the one already seen.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: DI-7.3: a pump asks whether the drain made entries poppable another way
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the new module: map_or(false, ..) is is_some_and(..), so this must survive; if it comes back caught, something is matching incidental text.

sabotages.name: DI-7.5: a pump does not drain before it waits
sabotages.why: The notification is an edge: the completions that raised it may have been taken by another waiter on the same event, and waiting for a raising that has happened blocks while they sit in the backend.

sabotages.name: DI-7.5: a pump whose first drain delivered reports none
sabotages.why: A first drain that delivered returns that it did, which sets the readiness event and tells the consumer to pop.
